## HueMux v0.0.1 — first tagged release

HueMux is a lightweight, cross-platform frontend for Philips Hue: a single
Go binary you drive from a browser or an optional Electron desktop window,
combining real-time screen-color sync to a Hue Entertainment area with
day-to-day light control — no cloud, no official Hue Sync app, no
platform-specific screen-capture hacks. This is the first tagged build;
everything below reflects what's actually in this binary today, not the
long-term roadmap.

### Core features

**Screen sync**
- Captures your screen and streams it to a Hue Entertainment area over
  DTLS 1.2, direct to the bridge, in real time.
- Four sampling modes — `edges`, `quadrant`, `global`, `spread` — picked
  with a sensible per-area default from the area's own `configuration_type`.
- Per-area zone mapping: which physical axis (x/y/z) from the Hue app's own
  room layout becomes screen-horizontal, screen-vertical, and "depth" is
  configurable and independently invertible, with depth scaling how large a
  region a light samples rather than positioning it.
- Reactivity (temporal smoothing window, 0–1200ms), brightness (0–200%),
  saturation, black cutoff, edge width, and letterbox (black-bar) detection,
  all persisted per entertainment area.
- Works natively on Wayland, X11, Windows, and macOS — no
  platform-specific capture code beyond the standard `getDisplayMedia()`
  Web API (plus an Electron-side PipeWire feature switch on Wayland).

**Light control**
- Every room and light on the bridge, grouped by room, with a per-room bulk
  tile (toggle/brightness/colour for the whole room) alongside individual
  light cards.
- Scenes with real colour-swatch previews and a dynamic-scene indicator,
  grouped under their room, or in their own section when tied to an
  entertainment zone instead.
- Favorites — lights, rooms, scenes, or "all lights" as one unit — for
  one-tap access.
- Sync and light control share one connection and can run at the same
  time from different tabs/windows without fighting over the stream.

**Platform**
- One Go binary for the core (`huemux`); an optional Electron wrapper
  (`huemux-desktop`) for a real window with no browser capture-picker
  dialog, with a `--headless` flag that's byte-for-byte the plain binary.
- CLI subcommands for scripting/diagnosis: `pair`, `areas`, `test` (a DTLS
  smoke test independent of any capture/UI).
- `-debug` writes a single timestamped log file capturing the *entire*
  process's output — not just app log lines, but stdout, stderr, and even
  an unrecovered panic — so a bug report needs one attachment, not a
  multi-step log gather.
- English and Polish UI, light/dark theme (system-following or manual).
- The server binds `127.0.0.1` only and checks WebSocket `Origin` — no
  authentication by design, since nothing but this loopback-bound process
  should ever reach it.

### Known bugs

- **Solid green (or black) screen-sync preview on the first sync attempt**
  under the Electron desktop build, most often on Wayland. A second attempt
  sometimes works. Root-caused via a live debugging session to a
  system-level PipeWire/GPU/portal issue on the affected machine, not a
  HueMux or Electron bug — see
  [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/blob/main/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)
  for the full writeup, what's already been ruled out, and what to check on
  your own system if you hit it.
- The Electron desktop build always captures the **primary screen only** —
  there's no source/monitor picker (the browser build gets one for free
  from the OS/browser's own `getDisplayMedia()` dialog). A real picker for
  the desktop build is a natural follow-up, not yet implemented.

### Compared to the official Hue apps

HueMux is not trying to be a full replacement for the Hue app or Hue Sync —
it covers the "sync my screen and flip my lights from my computer, locally"
slice. What it does differently or not at all, compared to the official
apps:

| Area | Official Hue app / Hue Sync | HueMux v0.0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Platform | Hue Sync: Windows/macOS only, no Linux. Hue app: iOS/Android (+ limited web) | Linux, Windows, macOS — browser or desktop, no mobile app |
| Connectivity | Cloud + local; remote (out-of-home) control | Local network only, direct to bridge — no cloud, no remote access |
| Entertainment areas | Create/edit 3D room layout in-app | Uses areas already created in the Hue app; cannot create or edit one |
| Sync sources | Screen, HDMI (via Sync Box hardware), music/audio-reactive | Screen only — no audio-reactive mode, no Sync Box hardware support |
| Multi-monitor source picker | Yes (Hue Sync) | Browser build: yes, via the OS/browser picker. Desktop build: no — primary screen only (see Known bugs) |
| Automations / routines / schedules | Yes (time, geofence, sensor-triggered) | Not implemented |
| Voice assistant integration (Alexa, Google, Siri/HomeKit) | Yes | Not implemented — out of scope, this isn't a bridge-side feature |
| Matter | Yes | Not implemented — out of scope, same reason |
| Multi-bridge support | Yes | One paired bridge per running instance |
| Guest access / multi-user permissions | Yes | Not implemented — single set of local bridge credentials |
| Firmware updates (bridge/bulbs) | Yes | Not implemented — use the official Hue app for this |
| Hue Labs / formulas | Yes | Not implemented |
| Rooms, lights, scenes, favorites | Yes | Yes |
| Cost / openness | Free apps, closed source | Free, open source (MIT + OFL font) |

### Installing

Download the binary for your platform from this release's assets below, or
build from source — see the
[README](https://github.com/zamber/huemux#readme). First run walks you
through pairing with your bridge; no terminal required unless you want the
CLI subcommands.

### Contributing / reporting bugs

Please use the **Debug log** field in the
[bug report template](https://github.com/zamber/huemux/issues/new/choose)
if you hit a problem — running with `-debug` and attaching the resulting
file is the fastest way to get a real bug triaged.
